title: Naming Intervals by Ear
description: Hear two notes and name the gap between them, with a few famous tunes to help.

steps.title: Two notes, one gap
steps.description:
You'll hear two notes, one after the other. Your job is to name the distance between them.

The trick most musicians use is to tie each interval to the opening of a song they already know. If the first two notes of a tune match what you hear, you've got your answer. Play each one as many times as you like.

steps.title: First pair
steps.description: Listen to the two notes. What's the interval?
steps.hint: Sing the opening of 'Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star'. Does 'Twin-kle, twin-kle' match?

steps.title: Second pair
steps.description: A smaller jump this time. What do you hear?
steps.hint: It sounds bright. Try the first two notes of 'When the Saints Go Marching In', on 'Oh, when'.

steps.title: Third pair
steps.description: Close to the last one, but listen to the mood. Which interval is it?
steps.hint: A touch darker than the last one. Think of the first two notes of 'Greensleeves'.

steps.title: Fourth pair
steps.description: What interval do you hear now?
steps.hint: Hum 'Here Comes the Bride'. Do the first two notes fit?

steps.title: A big leap
steps.description: This one jumps a long way. What's the interval?
steps.hint: Do the two notes sound like the same note, just higher? Think of 'Some-where' in 'Somewhere Over the Rainbow'.

steps.title: New starting note
steps.description: This pair starts somewhere else, which makes it harder. What do you hear?
steps.hint: You've already heard this distance in this lesson, just starting from a different note. Try your song tricks again.
